articles.title: Ranking the 10 Biggest NFL Draft Mistakes of the Past Decade
articles.summary: J.J. McCarthy's short-lived tenure with the Minnesota Vikings is officially over. Two years after the Vikings traded up to acquire him, they shipped the third-year signal-caller to the New York Giants for a fifth-round pick.
articles.body:
J.J. McCarthy's short-lived tenure with the Minnesota Vikings is officially over . Two years after the Vikings traded up to acquire him, they shipped the third-year signal-caller to the New York Giants for a fifth-round pick.

The fact that McCarthy was behind Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz on the Vikings' depth chart was the writing on the wall. But the Vikings trading him to the Giants for a middling Day 3 pick cemented his status as a historic draft mistake.

Was he the biggest gaffe of the past decade? That's what we're here to sort out.

It's especially damaging when teams whiff on top-10 picks, but that's not the only reason why McCarthy is a massive draft mistake. He played poorly, didn't earn a second contract with the Vikings, and great players were selected soon after him.

Luckily for the Vikings, he's hardly the only player who fits that mold over the past decade.

Although every player drafted since 2017 was eligible for these rankings, no one from the last two drafts made the cut because the sample size is still too small.

We begin with the Arizona Cardinals, who had two players in consideration for this spot in Simmons and 2018 No. 10 overall pick Josh Rosen. Simmons earned the nod for being a slightly higher pick and getting less draft capital back in his eventual trade.

Simmons played three seasons with the Cardinals before being dealt for a seventh-round pick.

No player drafted immediately after Simmons emerged as a surefire Pro Bowler either, but the Cardinals could have gone with Tristan Wirfs (No. 13), CeeDee Lamb (No. 17) or Justin Jefferson (No. 22) at that same spot.

Anthony Richardson showed tantalizing traits during his college career at Florida, albeit across only 13 starts. His career completion percentage was 54.7 percent, but hey, Josh Allen's was just 56.2 in college, and look how that worked out for the Buffalo Bills.

So, the Colts gambled that they could fix Richardson's accuracy issues in the NFL. However, it quickly became clear that they made a mistake when he completed only 47.7 percent of his pass attempts across 11 starts in his second season.

Richardson is still on the Colts, who would presumably trade him for a late-round pick if another team offered them one.

There wasn't a quarterback on the board whom the Colts should have taken instead, but they did pass on star cornerback Devon Witherspoon (No. 5 pick), running back Bijan Robinson (No. 8 pick) and defensive tackle Jalen Carter (No. 9 pick) for Richardson.

Taking a cornerback in the top five of the draft is usually reserved for generational prospects. Among the success stories are Deion Sanders (1989), Charles Woodson (1998), Patrick Peterson (2011) and Jalen Ramsey (2016).

Okudah had a great college career at Ohio State, but he was never considered the type of athlete that those four were. The Lions took him with the No. 3 overall pick in the 2020 draft anyway.

Three years later, they essentially admitted they made a mistake by trading him for a fifth-round pick before his fourth season began.

Okudah doesn't rank higher than this because no generational prospects came off the board within the next few picks. The closest is defensive tackle Derrick Brown, who was taken seventh overall.

Preseason Contenders in Desperation Mode

Harbaugh Reveals Giants QB1 After McCarthy Trade

This one hurts more than a typical top-10 bust. Most analysts considered Jalen Carter a better defensive lineman prospect than Tyree Wilson, but the Raiders passed on Carter to take Wilson.

It's understandable why Carter might have been " crossed off " their draft board, but now it's easy to say they made the wrong pick.

The Raiders traded Wilson and a seventh-round pick for a fifth-round pick before his fourth season. Meanwhile, Carter is a two-time Pro Bowler.

If the Raiders wanted to go in a different direction, they could've selected running backs Bijan Robinson (No. 8 pick) or Jahmyr Gibbs (No. 12 pick), cornerback Christian Gonzalez (No. 17 pick) or wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba (No. 20 pick).

Evan Neal was a disappointment in his four seasons with the New York Giants. They eventually released the offensive tackle during the 53-man roster cutdown ahead of the 2026 regular season.

The Giants used a 2026 first-round pick on tackle Francis Mauigoa, which gave Neal no shot at earning a starting role.

The Seattle Seahawks landed eventual Super Bowl-winning tackle Charles Cross two picks after the Giants took Neal, but that's not what makes this selection especially painful. It's that the next seven picks were all somewhere between good and excellent.

No. 8: WR Drake London No. 9: OT Charles Cross No. 10: WR Garrett Wilson No. 11: WR Chris Olave No. 12: WR Jameson Williams No. 13: DT Jordan Davis No. 14: S Kyle Hamilton

After giving up on Sam Darnold (more on him later), the New York Jets were in the market for another quarterback heading into the 2021 draft. Everyone expected them to take whichever of Trevor Lawrence or Zach Wilson fell to them at No. 2.

That's exactly what they did. They passed on Trey Lance, Justin Fields and Mac Jones to stand pat and take Wilson at No. 2.

As it turns out, all four QBs didn't pan out. So in that sense, it's hard to fault the Jets too much.

What the Jets needed to do was pivot to a player at any other position. Here are the non-QBs taken right after Wilson:

No. 4: TE Kyle Pitts No. 5: WR Ja'Marr Chase No. 6: WR Jaylen Waddle No. 7: OT Penei Sewell No. 8: CB Jaycee Horn No. 9: CB Patrick Surtain II No. 10: WR DeVonta Smith No. 12: OLB Micah Parsons No. 13: OT Rashawn Slater

At least they have... *checks notes*... Geno Smith back now?

Drafted: 10th overall, 2024 (after not-too-costly trade-up with Jets)

J.J. McCarthy lands at No. 4 in these rankings for two reasons.

First, the Minnesota Vikings passed on quarterback Bo Nix (No. 12 pick) as well as tight end Brock Bowers (No. 13 pick). It wasn't like McCarthy was a can't-miss prospect at Michigan, so it's fair to question why they didn't either a) go with the more experienced Nix or b) solve their quarterback problem a different way and take the generational tight end in Bowers.

Second, the Vikings are actually built perfectly for a QB to thrive with offensive mastermind Kevin O'Connell and wide receiver Justin Jefferson. This mistake has nothing to do with McCarthy's supporting cast.

In fact, Kirk Cousins went 13-4 and posted huge numbers in 2022 under this Minnesota regime, and Sam Darnold went 14-3 and posted huge numbers in 2024 while McCarthy was injured.

If the Vikings can hit on a quarterback in the draft, they should be a perennial Super Bowl contender. Their best shot at one was this pick, and they missed.

The Bears moved up from the third overall pick to the second overall pick by trading two third-rounders and a fourth-rounder to take Trubisky.

In four seasons in the Windy City, Trubisky wasn't awful. He even made one Pro Bowl and guided the Bears to two postseason appearances. But it's telling that Chicago let him walk in 2021 free agency before drafting Justin Fields.

Of course, we're burying the lead here. Trubisky ranks this high because the next quarterback taken in the 2017 draft was Patrick Mahomes at No. 10 overall.

In theory, every team that had a chance at Mahomes could be featured here. But the Bears deserve the most criticism for choosing a different quarterback over him.

The Jets paid a steep price to move up from No. 6 to No. 3 a month before the 2018 draft, giving up three second-round picks. It all ended up being up for a quarterback who didn't make it to a fourth season in New York.

Though the Jets got a second-round pick when they traded Darnold to the Carolina Panthers in 2021, it didn't make the wound feel much better.

What makes this mistake even more painful is that the Buffalo Bills took Josh Allen with the No. 7 pick of the 2018 draft.

Imagine how different the AFC East would have looked over the past decade had the Jets taken Allen instead of Darnold.

This was the clear-cut answer for the No. 1 spot in these rankings. It has as much to do with the San Francisco 49ers' process as the pick itself.

The Niners wanted to move up from the 12th pick to take a quarterback, but they weren't sure which one they wanted. Despite not knowing, they gave up first-round picks in 2022 and 2023 and a 2022 third-round pick to move up from No. 12 to No. 3 a month before the draft.

The player whom they reportedly originally wanted , Mac Jones, ended up being available at No. 12. But at some point, head coach Kyle Shanahan decided he wanted Trey Lance instead of Jones.

Lance had been getting first-round hype, but it's possible he would've been available at No. 12 as well. After all, he started only one season at North Dakota State and had plenty of questions about the caliber of competition he faced in college.

Lance started just four games in his two years with the Niners before they traded him to the Dallas Cowboys for a fourth-round pick.

A whiff like that can lead to the firing of a head coach and GM, but Shanahan and John Lynch avoided the hot seat by drafting Brock Purdy with the last pick of 2022 draft. He went from Mr. Irrelevant to an MVP candidate.

Still, you have to wonder whether the 49ers would have won a Super Bowl in the last few years had they stayed put in the 2021 draft. They could have used those first-round picks in 2022 and 2023 to address their weaknesses.

articles.title: 5 Trade Landing Spots That Would Rejuvenate Brian Thomas Jr.'s NFL Career
articles.summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars may be off to a hot start, but Brian Thomas Jr. remains mired in a slump.
articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars may be off to a hot start, but Brian Thomas Jr. remains mired in a slump.

Hopes that BTJ will return to his elite rookie form appear to be fading, prompting speculation that the Jaguars could consider trading the young wide receiver.

Although the Jags reportedly turned down " significant " trade offers for Thomas last year, they may not be so quick to rebuff any suitors that emerge in the coming weeks.

After recording a modest 80 yards on six catches over the first two weeks, Thomas had his quietest outing yet in Week 3. He led the Jaguars with nine targets in their Week 2 loss to the Denver Broncos, but his involvement dropped sharply the following week. Trevor Lawrence targeted him just once on Sunday.

While Thomas has been struggling, the Jags have been thriving. Following a statement 35-6 victory over the New England Patriots, Jacksonville moved to 2-1 and is again sitting atop the AFC South standings.

With wideouts like Parker Washington (15 catches for 221 yards and two touchdowns) and Jakobi Meyers (10 catches for 132 yards and two touchdowns) picking up the slack, Thomas can be considered expendable. Shipping the 2024 first-round pick off for draft capital and/or players who can contribute to the team's current Super Bowl push is shaping up to be the best outcome for all parties.

The Jags have until the November 10 trade deadline to make a decision on Thomas, but they may want to expedite moving the receiver before his value further plummets.

BTJ has proved he can be a superstar-level talent in the NFL during an 87-catch, 1,282-receiving yard, 10-touchdown rookie season, but a disappointing 48/707/2 line in 2025—coupled with his performance over the first three weeks of 2026—has severely hindered his stock.

With that in mind, here are five landing spots that would benefit Thomas most and allow him to reignite his career.

Brian Thomas Jr. could become the latest talented receiver to thrive under San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan.

A trade could be mutually beneficial: The Niners could use another impact wideout, while Thomas could benefit from a fresh start in a more receiver-friendly offense.

The 49ers have become downright desperate for serviceable bodies after a rash of injuries ravaged their roster throughout training camp and the start of the 2026 campaign. The receiving corps has been hit particularly hard, with Mike Evans becoming the most recent San Francisco pass-catcher to pick up an injury.

While Evans is considered day-to-day with a rib issue, the Niners have no insurance plan if they lose another wideout for an extended stretch. Ricky Pearsall is out for the season with a PCL injury, while rookie De'Zhaun Stribling will be out another two-plus months after suffering an ankle injury in the opener. DeMarcus Robinson landed on the IR last week due to a high-ankle sprain and Christian Kirk has yet to make his San Francisco debut due to a calf issue.

Considering Deebo Samuel, Jacob Cowing, Jordan Watkins and Khadarel Hodge are the only remaining healthy wideouts on the 49ers' roster, the team should be rushing to make a splash in the trade market. Taking Thomas off Jacksonville's hands may be risky, but it's also a high-reward maneuver that could pay dividends if the receiver eventually shines in Shanahan's offense.

It might take some time for Thomas to get brought up to speed in the system and build rapport with quarterback Brock Purdy, but the potential payoff of having another legitimate No. 1-caliber wideout in the fold come playoff time is worth the cost.

The Los Angeles Rams haven't looked like the heavy Super Bowl favorites they were entering the 2026 NFL season.

With the team off to an ugly 1-2 start and injuries mounting, a trade for underperforming but potential-laden wideout Brian Thomas Jr. seems far more palatable than it did at the onset of the campaign.

Puka Nacua was a major part of L.A.'s success in 2025, but the two-time Pro Bowler hasn't suited up since Week 1 due to a groin injury. While Davante Adams is still healthy, the team has been forced to lean on depth options such as unheralded sophomore Konata Mumpfield and veteran Tutu Atwell to try to generate passing offense.

Nacua's injury absence has also prompted contract-related speculation. Pro Football Talk's Mike Florio suggested Nacua "quite possibly" would be playing if he had received a new deal this offseason, though neither Nacua nor the Rams has publicly tied his return timeline to his contract situation.

Nacua's injury has exposed the Rams' need for more proven depth at wide receiver. Thomas could give Los Angeles another high-upside option alongside Davante Adams while Nacua is out, then serve as an overqualified third receiver when the group is healthy.

Perhaps most importantly, Thomas could slot into the organization's long-term plans.

Despite his struggles over the past season-plus, he won't turn 24 until October 8 and has yet to reach his peak in the NFL. He could emerge as the ideal runningmate for Nacua in the receiving corps once the team transitions into a new era without aging stars like Adams and quarterback Matt Stafford.

The upside for Thomas to not only greatly help the Rams contend in 2026, but also well beyond makes him worth the cost of admission. For a capital-strapped club that is all-in on lifting the Lombardi Trophy this year but still has aspirations to contend well into the future, there's hardly a better move to be made.

The New England Patriots should be in panic mode after they were on the receiving end of a Jacksonville Jaguars' shellacking on Sunday.

The loss dropped the team to 1-2, with the passing offense looking particularly abysmal for the third consecutive week.

With marquee offseason acquisition A.J. Brown on the shelf with a high-ankle sprain for several more weeks, the Pats shouldn't hesitate to make a bold trade for Brian Thomas Jr. to shore up the receiving corps.

The depth that New England appeared to have going into the 2026 NFL season hasn't materialized, with veterans like Mack Hollins (12/156/0 on 16 targets) and Romeo Doubs (6/145/0 on 11 targets) underwhelming in expanded roles.

The departures of veteran star Stefon Diggs—who led New England with 85 catches and 1,013 receiving yards last year—and deep threat Kayshon Boutte (33/551/6 in 2025) are being sorely felt around Foxboro.

While Brown can still be the No. 1 receiver this offense sorely needs when he returns from IR, quarterback Drake Maye desperately needs more weapons to get back to playing at an MVP level.

Although the Pats managed to bottle up Thomas when they faced him in Week 3, the coaching staff has assuredly seen the wideout's tremendous rookie tape and is aware of his upside.

A change of scenery, as well as working with one of the game's best young signal-callers, could be all BTJ needs to get his career back on track.

The Las Vegas Raiders have become unexpected contenders in the wake of a sizzling 3-0 start to the 2026 NFL season.

Although it initially seemed like this rebuilding club would be one of the league's sellers during the leadup to the trade deadline, Vegas now has to give serious credence to using draft capital to bring in assets like Brian Thomas Jr. to help with a playoff push.

The Raiders have struck gold with veteran Kirk Cousins leading their offense, but there is still room for improvement. Vegas' wideouts in particular stand out for not playing up to the same level the rest of this offense has achieved.

Although four players on the team have recorded at least 10 catches, 87 receiving yards and a receiving touchdown, Tre Tucker (11/189/1 on 15 targets) is the only wide receiver to stand among that group.

Jalen Nailor has been the Raiders' second-most prolific wideout, but he's only contributed a modest five catches for 52 yards on his 11 targets. Cody White leads the team with three touchdown catches, but has just three total catches on the year.

There is plenty of room for another receiver in Sin City, with Thomas making sense to fill that role.

Although Cousins has completed 67.4 percent of his throws for 661 yards and a league-high nine touchdowns over the first three weeks, he could be even more prolific with a true No. 1 wideout in the fold.

At his best, Thomas showed he can handle a feature role thanks to a rare blend of size, speed, athleticism and catching ability. Although he hasn't consistently displayed that talent since the end of his rookie campaign, the potential for him to return to form in Klint Kubiak's offense is truly alluring.

If the Raiders can get the 23-year-old wideout without mortgaging too much of their promising future, they shouldn't hesitate to make the move.

The Pittsburgh Steelers have proved to be a surprisingly plucky team in 2026, moving to 2-1 after a big Week 3 win over the Cincinnati Bengals.

While the club is now atop the AFC North standings, every team in the division boasts the same record and has a real chance at claiming the crown.

Because of how fierce this AFC North race is shaping up to be, the Steelers can't afford to rest on their laurels and must add more firepower. Aaron Rodgers has looked far more like a 43-year-old gritting through his final NFL season than the perennial MVP candidate of yore, but bolstering his weapons could help change that.

Brian Thomas Jr. could be the best bang for Pittsburgh's buck, providing them with a potential WR1 at a budget cost.

The Steelers' receiving corps has been lackluster outside of Roman Wilson, who surprisingly paces the unit with 11 catches, 114 receiving yards and one receiving touchdown on the year. D.K. Metcalf has been particularly disappointing—catching just 11 of his team-high 24 targets for 98 yards and a touchdown on the year—while key offseason pickup Michael Pittman Jr. (5/74/0 in the two games he's suited up for) looks washed.

With every wideout outside of Wilson failing to meet even modest expectations, Pittsburgh's brass must make a bold move on the trade market. Thomas may not be succeeding with the Jacksonville Jaguars, but his best football should still be ahead of him.

Getting to play with a 10-time Pro Bowl quarterback within an offense that is desperate for pass-catching assistance may be exactly what BTJ needs to turn things around.

At worst, the Steelers cough up a bit of capital for yet another underwhelming wideout who fails to pan out for them. At best, Thomas becomes the new No. 1 WR in Pittsburgh's offense and retains that role for multiple seasons.

A Thomas trade is worth the risk and could pay massive dividends for a Steelers squad looking to take the next step after years of mediocrity.

articles.title: Drake Maye isn't the same quarterback anymore, and the Patriots' early struggles are starting to explain why
articles.summary: Drake Maye has thrown six interceptions in three games, the most in the NFL, and the Patriots are 1-2 after a 35-6 loss at Jacksonville on Sunday.
articles.body: Drake Maye has thrown six interceptions in three games, the most in the NFL, and the Patriots are 1-2 after a 35-6 loss at Jacksonville on Sunday. The third-year quarterback added a fumble and two more picks against the Jaguars, and New England failed to score a touchdown in a loss for the first time in more than two seasons. Coach Mike Vrabel says he does not expect any lingering shoulder issue. Maye says he sees no shoulder problem, but he sidestepped direct questions about it. Buffalo, still unbeaten, is next in the AFC East opener.Is Drake Maye really not the same quarterback this season?The numbers say yes. Through three games, Drake Maye has one touchdown, six interceptions and 585 passing yards. At the same point last year, he had five touchdowns, two interceptions and 785 yards. He ended 2025 with 31 touchdowns and eight interceptions, so he has already thrown three-quarters of that total. His six picks are the most by a Patriots quarterback through three games since Drew Bledsoe threw eight in 1994.The bigger change is how he plays in the pocket. He has forced throws into tight coverage, overthrown receivers and taken nine sacks. He has also admitted that shaking off a bad play has been hard. "I've got to look myself in the mirror and take this as a turning point," he said. In the third quarter, Vrabel held Maye by the shoulders and spoke to him for a long stretch. Vrabel also said he wants Maye to be energetic and that he "can't be a robot here."The supporting cast has thinned too. Stefon Diggs is gone to Washington, and A.J. Brown has missed time since a high ankle sprain in Week 1. He is not expected back before late October. Without a receiver he trusts to get open fast, Maye has leaned on big plays downfield. The ground game has not eased the load. New England ran 26 times for 83 yards in Jacksonville, and the offense has scored just 29 points on 30 drives this season.Is a shoulder injury behind Drake Maye's slow start?Questions about the shoulder surfaced right after the loss, and they remain open. Drake Maye landed hard on his right shoulder against Denver in the AFC Championship Game in January. He then received a pain-relieving injection before Super Bowl LX, according to the Associated Press. He never had surgery, and no specific diagnosis has been made public.Vrabel said, "I don't anticipate that being any issue going forward." Maye said Sunday, "I wouldn't say there's a problem with my shoulder." On Monday, though, he answered three straight questions about how his arm feels by talking about execution. He has not appeared on an injury report this season.An injury would be the simplest explanation, but nothing confirms it, and the bad habits on tape look like decisions and timing. One number captures the slide. Since the start of last season's playoffs, Maye has nine fumbles and 10 interceptions in seven games. No one has reached both marks in a seven-game span since Jameis Winston in 2019.Maye has not yet given the one clean answer that would settle it. articles.title: Ollie Gordon II and the Best Week 4 Fantasy Football Waiver-Wire Pickups
articles.summary: The 2026 fantasy football season has been a chaotic one, rife with major injuries that have shaken up the NFL landscape and left many managers desperately searching for suitable replacements on waivers.
articles.body:
The 2026 fantasy football season has been a chaotic one, rife with major injuries that have shaken up the NFL landscape and left many managers desperately searching for suitable replacements on waivers.

Waiver claims won't always pan out—just ask those who scooped up Jonah Coleman early last week before it was revealed he had picked up an ankle injury that required a stint on the IR—but it's still the best tool managers have at their disposal to win leagues.

Even if your team has survived this rash of injuries relatively unscathed, late September remains an ideal time to review lineups and make adjustments.

At this point in the season, sleepers who have stayed asleep instead of breaking out can be safely dropped. It may not be time to completely divest yourself of underwhelming early-to-mid-round draft selections, but sending them to the bench while turning over the bottom of the roster in exchange for high-upside talent off waivers will pay dividends down the line.

There are plenty of intriguing free agents who remain widely available, so read on for some advice on which players you should be targeting on waivers ahead of Week 4.

Suggestions are available in approximately half or more of all Yahoo! Sports leagues. Fantasy points and rankings courtesy of FantasyPros' PPR data. Suggested free-agent acquisition budget (FAAB) bids are based on a $100 starting budget.

Sam Darnold, Seattle Seahawks (37 Percent Rostered)

Darnold wasted little time knocking off the rust after he returned to the field following a two-week absence. While the Seahawks failed to pick up a win against the Washington Commanders, their signal-caller went off for 29.7 fantasy points in the 33-31 decision.

While Darnold still needs to prove he can put together these types of explosive outings on a regular basis—his top-five finish was his first since Week 14 of last season and just the fourth he's posted since signing with Seattle—the QB is a completely serviceable fantasy starter now that he's healthy.

Considering Darnold is lacking the same level of rushing support he had last year, it wouldn't be a shock if he's tasked with airing it out a bit more frequently. With 45 throws on Sunday, he tallied his most passing attempts in a game since his 2019 rookie campaign with the New York Jets.

With a vulnerable Los Angeles Chargers defense that both Jacoby Brissett and Kirk Cousins have already shredded this season on tap in Week 4, Darnold could be in for another big day.

Geno Smith, New York Jets (9 Percent Rostered)

A return to the Big Apple has been a massive boon to Smith's career. Although expectations were low going into 2026, the quarterback has kept the Jets competitive in all three of their contests. He wasn't moving the fantasy needle during the first two games, but a top-five showing in Week 3 has the veteran passer back in the low-end QB1 discussion.

Smith dissected the Detroit Lions defense on Sunday, connecting on 31 of his 37 throws for 321 yards and three touchdowns with zero interceptions. While he did lose a fumble, he still finished with a strong 26.0 fantasy points.

Another top-10 outing could be in store for Smith when Gang Green visits the Chicago Bears in Week 4. The Bears struggled to contain opposing quarterbacks over the first two weeks of the 2026 season before clamping down on Jalen Hurts in Week 3, so there's a decent chance this upcoming clash turns into a shootout.

Cousins is doing far more than serving as a temporary bridge quarterback for Fernando Mendoza. While the No. 1 overall pick will inevitably inherit the keys to this offense, the veteran is keeping the rookie at bay with a stellar stretch to open the 2026 campaign.

Although Cousins hasn't been putting up mind-blowing fantasy numbers during Vegas' 3-0 start to the season, he's established himself as a decent starter in the wake of back-to-back top-12 finishes. He leads the league with nine touchdown passes—throwing three in each game—and those scores shouldn't slow too much in the coming weeks.

You can't count on Cousins to work as a season-long starter, but those in need of a budget rental can fire up the 38-year-old with confidence as long as he remains the Raiders' starter.

Ollie Gordon II, Miami Dolphins (4 Percent Rostered)

Gordon is your top waiver-wire target for Week 4. The Dolphins back projects to see a massive uptick in volume with De'Von Achane ruled out for the rest of the 2026 season and should be rostered in nearly every format.

After Achane went down with a torn ACL early in a Week 3 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs, Gordon became Miami's lead back and contributed a respectable 41 rushing yards and a touchdown on 17 totes. He also showed some skills in the passing game, adding 14 receiving yards on three catches.

Because fellow backup Jaylen Wright was inactive with a foot injury, Gordon was the only Miami backfield member to touch the football outside of Achane on Sunday.

Jaylen Wright could take on part of the workload, though Miami may prefer to use a committee rather than give either back a true feature role.

Gordon has potential to be a significant fantasy asset for that projected volume alone.

Those in deeper leagues may want to snap up Wright as well, but Gordon is the Dolphins rusher to roster if you can only make room for one. The bruising back is a decent bet to emerge as a low-end RB2, high-end RB3 for the remainder of the 2026 campaign.

Braelon Allen, New York Jets (19 Percent Rostered)

In the wake of Breece Hall's scary quad injury, Allen becomes one of the main waiver-wire draws for Week 4. The backup running back has potential to seamlessly slide into the starter's role and put up similar numbers in an offense that has been clicking as of late.

Allen hasn't seen much work to open the 2026 season—totaling just 13.2 fantasy points across his first three games—but that is poised to change while Hall is set to be sidelined for a stretch.

While it hasn't been confirmed exactly how long Hall will be out for, the back ominously stated after Sunday's 31-24 defeat to the Detroit Lions that "I felt something when I was running and then got tackled and planted and then felt something else."

Initial reports are that Hall has avoided a season-ending injury, but he's still being considered week-to-week and is highly unlikely to play against the Chicago Bears on Sunday.

Hall had posted RB12 and RB16 finishes in his first two games of the year, logging a team-high 45 touches in that span. Considering New York was content utilizing a two-man platoon that saw Hall garner the lion's share of touches, Allen should assume most of the volume in any game Hall misses, with Isaiah Davis moving up a rung on the depth chart to handle backup duties.

Allen should be considered a potential RB2 for Weeks 4 and 5. He may not be a league-winner, but he's still worth utilizing a decent chunk of FAAB dollars or a high waiver priority to acquire for managers desperate for short-term RB help.

Alvin Kamara, New Orleans Saints (43 Percent Rostered)

The Saints' decision to sign Travis Etienne Jr. hasn't been paying off. With the pricey running back underwhelming over the first two games and picking up a hamstring injury just after halftime in Week 3, the stage is set for Alvin Kamara to retake control of this platoon.

While Kamara has been dealing with injuries of his own and missed Week 1, he's racked up 63 yards on 24 touches since making his 2026 debut. Those are far from the contributions managers will want to see from a player they'd consider placing in their starting lineup, but there is room for Kamara to vastly improve.

With head coach Kellen Moore confirming that Etienne will miss some time , Kamara becomes the next man up in New Orleans' backfield. Expect Kamara to see a noticeable bump in both offensive snap count and volume, giving him plug-and-play potential in what could be a high-scoring Week 4 battle against the Atlanta Falcons.

Keenan Allen, Indianapolis Colts (21 Percent Rostered)

The Colts' already-thin receiving corps took a major hit when Alec Pierce's nagging heel injury forced him on the IR leading up to the team's Week 3 showdown with the Houston Texans. Despite missing their top wideout, Indy still secured its first win of the 2026 NFL season thanks to an impressive showing from Allen.

While Allen had a relatively quiet start to the year (finishing as the WR38 and WR110 in his first two games in a Colts uniform), the 34-year-old showed he can still provide valuable fantasy production by reeling in six of his nine targets for 63 yards and a touchdown.

His 18.3 fantasy points and WR17 finish marked his best showing since a vintage 11-catch, 119-receiving yard, one-touchdown outing against Indianapolis in Week 7 of last year.

Allen managed to turn back the clock against a stingy Houston secondary, suggesting he's plenty capable of another big performance when the Colts square off with the sieve-like Washington Commanders defense in Week 4.

The Commanders have allowed a league-high 31.5 fantasy points per game to opposing WRs in 2026, making Allen the type of waiver target who can immediately slot into your starting lineup if you land him.

Wan'Dale Robinson, Tennessee Titans (47 Percent Rostered)

The Titans' dreadful offensive display that opened the 2026 season led Robinson to become available in most leagues ahead of Week 3. Dropping the diminutive possession receiver proved to be a misstep by managers who went on to watch Robinson have a vintage PPR explosion against his former team on Sunday.

Robinson was one of Tennessee's only productive players in a disheartening 12-7 loss to the New York Giants, bringing in seven of his team-high 11 targets for 57 yards and a touchdown. His 18.7 points were his most as a Titan so far, but he's been no stranger to top-20 finishes. Dating back to Week 12 of last season, Robinson has placed in the top-20 in four of the eight contests he's suited up for.

Although the 0-3 Titans need to tinker with their offense and try to find a way to get Cam Ward going, Robinson should remain a major part of the team's plans and has plenty of flex appeal going into a Week 4 bout with the Baltimore Ravens.

Jakobi Meyers, Jacksonville Jaguars (44 Percent Rostered)

The Jaguars' pecking order has been fluid to open the 2026 NFL season, but a clearer picture is starting to emerge after their big Week 3 win over the New England Patriots.

Parker Washington is clearly the top option after his explosive stretch to open the year, but Meyers also seems to be back on the fantasy radar following an up-and-down start to the year.

After logging just three targets across the first two games, the Jags got Meyers more involved on Sunday. It resulted in a season-best performance that included seven catches, 64 receiving yards and one touchdown on eight looks.

Meyers has earned the right to be the No. 2 option in Jacksonville's passing attack, outperforming a slumping Brian Thomas Jr.—who was relegated to a rotational role after he caught just three of his nine targets in Week 2—and rookie Josh Cameron. As long as he continues to see the 80-plus percent offensive snap share he's earned over the past two weeks, Meyers will be a starting-caliber fantasy option.

Mack Hollins, New England Patriots (3 Percent Rostered)

The Patriots were dealt a major blow when A.J. Brown went down with a high-ankle sprain. While the team is struggling mightily without its No. 1 wideout, Mack Hollins has jumped out as the main fantasy football beneficiary.

Hollins has hardly come off the field since Brown went down with the ankle issue. He had his best game yet in Week 3, securing six of nine targets for 87 yards. While he's yet to find pay dirt in 2026, it's only a matter of time before he scores with this type of volume.

Don't expect Hollins to continue seeing such a heavy workload once Brown returns, but with New England's WR1 on the shelf until Week 6 at the earliest, fantasy managers can still extract some decent value from this waiver claim.

Kenyon Sadiq, New York Jets (18 Percent Rostered)

After flirting with TE1 status in the opener, Sadiq finally lived up to his first-round billing with a breakout performance. The rookie went off against the Detroit Lions on Sunday, amassing 23.5 fantasy points in a 31-24 defeat.

Sadiq is quickly establishing himself as a go-to target for quarterback Geno Smith. The 21-year-old posted a 7/105/1 line in Week 3, coming in behind only star wideout Garrett Wilson in terms of looks, catches and receiving yardage in the contest.

Despite missing a large portion of the offseason with injury, Sadiq is already starting to produce at a high level. He's only scratching the surface of his immense potential and should only improve with more reps in this offense.

Any fantasy manager who has been dealing with injuries or ineffective play from their drafted tight ends should consider Sadiq a priority target on waivers ahead of Week 4. You won't get many more opportunities this season to put a claim in on a potential high-end TE1 who can be started on a weekly basis.

Darren Waller, Carolina Panthers (14 Percent Rostered)

Waller surprisingly showed he could be more than a touchdown-dependent fantasy contributor in Week 3.

After generating some waiver wire buzz following his three-catch, 14-receiving yard, two-touchdown performance the prior week, the veteran tight end managed another double-digit fantasy point day despite failing to find the end zone in Carolina's 21-18 defeat to the Cleveland Browns.

Due to a rash of injuries to the Panthers' crop of pass-catchers, Waller wound up playing a much larger role than the one he assumed over the first two weeks of the campaign. He tallied his highest volume of offensive snaps (39), targets, receptions and receiving yardage since joining the club and could continue to build on those now that top receiver Jalen Coker has joined fellow wideout Xavier Legette on the injury report.

Terrance Ferguson, Los Angeles Rams (37 Percent Rostered)

Ferguson remains up for grabs in most leagues despite his strong Week 2 showing against the Baltimore Ravens.

An ankle injury picked up in Sunday night's loss to the Denver Broncos ruined any chances of building on that TE8 finish, but Ferguson is still worth stashing for his upside at a position that largely lacks stable contributors in fantasy football.

With Puka Nacua dealing with a nagging groin injury, there are plenty of targets up for grabs in L.A.'s offense. The team picked up its lone victory of the 2026 season in a contest Ferguson showed out in and should get the sophomore tight end heavily involved whenever he returns to the field.

Although Ferguson is facing an uphill battle to return for a Week 4 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles, he's avoided an IR stint and could be good to insert into your starting lineup when the Rams meet the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football the following week.

articles.title: Russell Wilson and Ciara built a $13 million charity foundation, turning NFL stardom into a mission focused on children and communities
articles.summary: Russell Wilson and Ciara have built a charity foundation reported to be worth $13 million, and its focus is on children and local communities.
articles.body: Russell Wilson and Ciara have built a charity foundation reported to be worth $13 million, and its focus is on children and local communities. The Why Not You Foundation began in 2014, when Wilson was a young quarterback in Seattle. Ciara has since become a central partner in the work. Together they raise money for kids facing illness, poverty and limited opportunity. The money comes from galas, sponsors and everyday donors, not just one athlete's salary. For a player still active in the NFL, the foundation has grown into a second career with real weight of its own.How did Russell Wilson and Ciara build a $13 million charity foundation?The story starts with Russell Wilson's father, Harrison Wilson III, who died in 2010. Wilson has said many times that his dad pushed him with a simple question: why not you? That question became the foundation's name. He launched it in 2014, the same year he won a Super Bowl with the Seahawks.The early work was personal. During his Seattle years, Wilson visited patients at Seattle Children's Hospital week after week, often on his day off. Those visits gave the charity a face long before it had big numbers.Ciara changed the scale. The couple married in 2016, and she brought her own audience, plus years of experience with large public events. Fans who never watch football now hear about the foundation through her. That matters, because a $13 million total rarely comes from one athlete's paycheck. It builds from sponsors, event tickets, auction bids and small gifts that add up over time.Their names also open doors. Corporate partners and other celebrities tend to say yes when both Wilson and Ciara ask. Donors see two public figures who show up in person, which is harder to fake than a logo on a banner.There is a practical side too. A single fundraiser can bring in a big one-night sum, but steady giving depends on trust, and trust grows slowly.What does the Why Not You Foundation do for kids and communities?The stated focus is young people, especially children dealing with illness and those with limited access to education. Its programs have supported hospital care, youth education and community events. That spread can look scattered, but it fits how the Wilsons work. They pick up needs where they see them.Longevity is the real story here. Athlete charities often fade once a player changes teams or retires. Wilson has played for Seattle, Denver and Pittsburgh, and the foundation kept working through each move. That kind of steadiness is rare, and it is easier to praise than to maintain. The NFL noticed too. In 2020 he won the Walter Payton Man of the Year award, the league's top honor for off-field service.Readers who want to judge the impact can do it themselves. Charity databases publish annual filings that show how much a foundation raises and how much reaches programs. That is the fair test for any celebrity cause, including this one.For the Wilsons, the next question is scale. A $13 million foundation can fund real projects, but it can't fix child poverty alone. Its best path is steady partnerships with schools, hospitals and local groups. articles.title: Jalen Hurts, Eagles on Wrong Side of NFL History With Rare Stat Loss to Bears
articles.summary: As if a 27-7 loss to the Chicago Bears wasn't bad enough, the Philadelphia Eagles also set a unique NFL record on Monday Night Football.
articles.body:
As if a 27-7 loss to the Chicago Bears wasn't bad enough, the Philadelphia Eagles also set a unique NFL record on Monday Night Football.

Per OptaSTATS, the Eagles became the first team ever have a game with fewer than 50 offensive plays, fewer than 250 total yards, commit at least three turnovers and 10 penalties with no takeaways or sacks.

Harbaugh Reveals Giants QB1 After McCarthy Trade

Preseason Contenders in Desperation Mode

That very granular-type of record does speak to some of the bigger issues that have already popped up on both sides of the ball for the Eagles this season. The defense, which was thought to be the strength of this roster, has yet to record a takeaway through three games.

The change in offensive coordinator from Kevin Patullo to Sean Mannion doesn't appear to have made much of a difference. Jalen Hurts' EPA per play of minus-0.04 ranks 27th out of 49 total quarterbacks through three weeks. His success rate of 41.4 percent ranks 30th, sandwiched between Carson Wentz and Bo Nix.

Saquon Barkley is averaging 5.1 yards per carry, but his down-to-down efficiency is a problem with a 38.2 percent success rate.

The Eagles have five turnovers this season, all of which have come in the last two games. Monday night saw them lose a fumble deep in their own territory, but the defense was able to hold after the Bears' fourth-and-goal pass attempt failed.

Andy Dalton, who had to play four snaps midway through the second quarter while Hurts was being evaluated for a concussion, threw a terrible interception in the end zone when he seemed not to see Bears safety Dillon Thieneman.

The Eagles now rank 23rd in points and 24th in yards per game. They were lucky to escape Week 2 with a win over the Tennessee Titans, then came out completely flat against a Bears team that didn't have Caleb Williams.

Now, with a 2-1 record, the Eagles' next two games are home against the Los Angeles Rams on a short week and at the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 5.

articles.title: Case Keenum Hyped by Bears HC Ben Johnson After Win vs. Eagles Amid Caleb Williams, Bagent Injuries
articles.summary: Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson showered third-string quarterback Case Keenum with praise after he led the Bears to a 27-7 home win over the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday night.
articles.body:
Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson showered third-string quarterback Case Keenum with praise after he led the Bears to a 27-7 home win over the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday night.

Speaking to reporters after the Bears' thoroughly dominant performance, Johnson said, "It's all about Case Keenum and what he was able to do here tonight. I thought he did an extraordinary job."

Keenum was given the game ball by Johnson, with the quarterback giving an emotional speech to the team (1:42 mark of the video):

Trade Landing Spots to Rejuvenate Brian Thomas Jr.'s Career 🛬

Seeing his first game action since 2023, Keenum didn't show any signs of rust, as he completed 24 of his 34 pass attempts for 247 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions, while also rushing for six yards and a score.

The rushing touchdown was perhaps the most surprising aspect of Keenum's night, as he hadn't had one of those since 2019.

Johnson joked with reporters, noting that he had previous experience calling offensive plays for quarterbacks who aren't necessarily fleet of foot, which was an obvious reference to Jared Goff of the Detroit Lions:

Multiple dominoes had to fall in order for Keenum to have the opportunity to start, and that is exactly what happened dating back to last week.

Franchise quarterback Caleb Williams injured his hamstring during the Bears' loss to the Minnesota Vikings last week, meaning backup Tyson Bagent was the next man up.

However, Bagent spent the week in concussion protocol and was only able to log one practice , so he dressed as the backup to Keenum.

The 38-year-old Keenum has extensive starting experience, going 31-36 in 67 career regular-season starts, while also making two playoff starts, but it was fair to wonder how he would fare after not playing any meaningful snaps in nearly three years.

Keenum was up for the challenge, though, and he may have played himself into position to continue starting until Williams is healthy enough to return.

articles.title: George Kittle gave more than $250,000 to military nonprofits and 400-plus tickets to heroes, building a charity legacy beyond football
articles.summary: George Kittle has donated more than $250,000 to military nonprofits and over 400 game tickets to service members and frontline heroes across six years.
articles.body: George Kittle has donated more than $250,000 to military nonprofits and over 400 game tickets to service members and frontline heroes across six years. The 49ers tight end was named the NFL's 2024 Salute to Service Award recipient, with the news coming in February 2025. The award, backed by USAA, recognizes members of the NFL family who support the military community. It was Kittle's fourth nomination by the 49ers. This time he beat two other finalists, including Vikings running back Aaron Jones. His record goes well beyond checks and tickets.How much has George Kittle given to military charities?The headline numbers are the $250,000 in donations and the 400-plus tickets. His giving and his My Cause My Cleats designs have supported groups such as the Pat Tillman Foundation, TAPS, Merging Vets and Players, Operation Freedom Paws and Operation Surf.The tickets are the part fans can picture. Kittle hosts military members and frontline heroes at every game. After games, win or lose, he holds a meet-and-greet with them. That detail matters. Giving away tickets is easy to do from a distance. Standing in a postgame line asks for time and energy when most players just want to go home. Six seasons of that routine says more than one large check would.There is a family story behind it. Kittle's uncle and grandfather both served. In his award statement, Kittle said, "My appreciation for the military stems from watching my Uncle Pat serve multiple tours with the National Guard and seeing firsthand how much it impacted him and his family while he was overseas."What else does George Kittle do for veterans beyond donations?Kittle and his family launched the Hidden Pearls Podcast in 2020 to share community stories. Nearly 60 of those stories involved veterans. The conversations led to something practical. The family built an app that offers free mental health resources to veterans, including the meditative practices Kittle uses while he plays.That app may say more than any donation total. Money supports a nonprofit's work. A free tool on a phone reaches a veteran directly, at any hour. It also connects to Kittle's own routine on the field, which makes it read as something personal, not a side project. He credits his family for making "these genuine and authentic relationships" possible.The award itself carries a payout. USAA will give $25,000 in Kittle's honor to the aid societies for each military branch. The NFL Foundation will match that amount for a military charity Kittle picks. NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said, "George Kittle truly embodies the essence of the Salute to Service Award."Kittle was quick to share the credit. "We are allowed to live the lives we live here because of the sacrifices they make, so we’re just trying to honor them, show our support, and share as much love as we can."He received the award at a private ceremony at Levi's Stadium after the 49ers played the Lions on Dec. 30, 2024. articles.title: NFL Panic Meter: With Baker Mayfield out, Bucs' backup plan at QB might wreck their season
articles.summary: Jalon Daniels is in a high-pressure spot over the next few weeks.
articles.body:
When the Tampa Bay Buccaneers decided that undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels had earned their backup quarterback job in August, they knew the risk involved.

Daniels was the first undrafted rookie in Buccaneers history to start the season as the team's primary backup quarterback. It was an unusual decision, but one the Bucs thought was right after training camp and a solid preseason. Daniels, who played six college seasons at Kansas, completed 27-of-44 passes for 239 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions with 37 yards and a touchdown on the ground in three preseason games.

The Buccaneers made that decision presumably hoping Daniels wouldn't be needed this season. Then, suddenly, he was.

Baker Mayfield dislocated his thumb late in the Buccaneers' loss to the Minnesota Vikings and coach Todd Bowles told WFLA he will miss "a minimum of three weeks." Bowles said Daniels will be the starter on Sunday against the Green Bay Packers .

It's obviously a very scary stretch coming up for the Buccaneers. They are 0-3 after a collapse in the second half of last season. They're 2-10 in their last 12 games. If Mayfield misses three games and the Bucs lose all three with Daniels (vs. Packers, at Cowboys , vs. Steelers ), they'll be 0-6 and 2-13 in their last 15. Bowles is already on the hot seat and an 0-6 start would be bad for him. It might also be bad for general manager Jason Licht, who put together the roster and didn't have a better backup quarterback plan than an undrafted rookie who was good but far from great at Kansas.

It's not inconceivable that Daniels could keep the Buccaneers afloat, though. The Pittsburgh Steelers won the first three starts of undrafted rookie Devlin "Duck" Hodges' career in 2019, though they lost the next three and Hodges didn't play in the NFL after that season. Tommy DeVito played well as an undrafted rookie for the 2023 New York Giants , they won three of his six starts and now he's the primary backup for the Patriots . Tyson Bagent got four starts as an undrafted rookie for the 2023 Bears , they went 2-2 and he's now their established backup.

So perhaps the idea of an 0-3 team having to start an undrafted rookie for a few weeks isn't as bad as it sounds. But it is a tough ask. And it was a risky proposition when the Buccaneers decided on it.

"You can go back and forth with the experience argument, but we'd rather have a very talented, prepared, inexperienced quarterback than going with experience just for the sake of saying the guy's experienced," Licht said via the team's site. "Like all rookie quarterbacks, whether you're the No. 1 overall pick or undrafted, there's going to be a learning curve, there's going to be ups and downs. But we feel good about where he's at, his trajectory, and we're excited."

We'll see if the Buccaneers can get through the next few games without Mayfield. If it goes terribly bad, there will be some justified consternation around the Buccaneers' offices.

Panic meter: Unless Daniels has a surprising run, this could get very ugly.

Maye hurt his shoulder in last season's AFC championship game, and it should be healed by now. But Maye has been so bad to start this season, there's some concern it's lingering.

And Maye's strange answers didn't exactly put the speculation to rest. He dodged the first question about his shoulder.

"I don't think that has anything to do with executing and playing better football and realizing that's the biggest thing that contributes to winning," Maye told WEEI, according to Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald .

Maye was asked a follow-up question and he gave the answer that most players give when they're playing through injury.

"Any time I'm out there, and I'm in uniform on the field, I'm gonna play 100% and give it my all," Maye said, via Kyed. "That's kind of what I have to say."

That is far from denying his shoulder is injured, when he had multiple opportunities to do so. At this point, an injury is the only logical way to explain how Maye can go from almost winning MVP last season to being one of the worst quarterbacks in the NFL through three games this season. It's worth monitoring now.

Panic meter: Maye's play is already alarming, and an injury possibility is now a curious part of that.

Bengals ' defense reverts to previous form

Through two weeks of the NFL season, one of the fun stories was the improvement of the Cincinnati Bengals' defense. After a few years being near the bottom of the league, it looked like the addition of Dexter Lawrence II and others might have turned things around during a 2-0 start.

Then the Steelers, who had scored one touchdown in two games before Sunday, dropped 30 points on the Bengals. Jaylen Warren ran all over them. Aaron Rodgers , at age 42, had nearly 300 yards passing. It looked like the past few seasons, when a leaky defense was the main reason the Bengals kept missing the playoffs. Everyone in Cincinnati would be in trouble if the Bengals miss the playoffs for a fourth straight season in Joe Burrow 's prime.

Panic meter: Cincinnati is better on defense, but maybe not as much as hoped.

Take any quarterback's No. 1 receiver away and his production will suffer. Stroud's has plummeted without Nico Collins .

That's not good news for Stroud. Houston scored six points without Collins in Week 2, then on Sunday, the Texans had seven points and 93 yards through three quarters against a Colts defense that was the worst in the NFL through two weeks. The Texans rallied a bit in the fourth quarter but lost 19-17 to fall to 0-3.

As Yahoo Sports' Jay Busbee wrote , it's not good for Stroud in a big season for his future. The Texans have to make a decision, whether to sign him to a big extension or not. ESPN's Jeremy Fowler wrote before the season started that the Texans were "prepared" to put Stroud in the $50 million per season club. One has to wonder if that offer is still on the table, or if there would be any offer at all if the Texans' season goes completely sour.

Panic meter: Houston has to be wondering if they have to start over at QB.

Through two games Achane had 38 touches. He was probably going to continue to get more, because the Dolphins are thin on offense. That's not an option anymore after Achane tore his ACL, ending his season .

The Dolphins are 31st in points scored and 26th in yardage gained, and that was with Achane for two full games. It will not get better without Achane, one of the most explosive players in the NFL. The Dolphins' list of skill-position players looks like something you'd see in the third preseason game. Good luck to QB Malik Willis .

Panic meter: There are going to be some ugly games for the Dolphins' offense.

The Rams' two losses are ugly. No way around that. In the first one, they were dominated in Australia by the 49ers . Even if we blame jet lag, they didn't play well. Then on Sunday, they blew a 16-0 halftime lead, giving up 30 points in the second half of a loss to the Denver Broncos . They're 1-2, two games (and the tiebreaker, for now) behind the 49ers in the NFC West.

What the Rams really need is health. Puka Nacua missed his second straight game with a groin injury and surgery isn't completely off the table, according to a report from ESPN . Myles Garrett is still out. Either of those players would have made a difference on Sunday, especially Garrett as the Rams couldn't get a stop (or a correct call on what was not a defensive pass interference ).

It has been three games. The Rams have played two of them without two of the NFL's best players. The Broncos loss came after the Rams outgained Denver by 225 yards. Don't let the record fool you.

Panic meter: Not much at all, assuming Nacua and Garrett get healthy.

articles.title: Eagles' Nick Sirianni Talks 'Remorse' For Reaction to Hit on Jalen Hurts After Viral Video
articles.summary: Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni is not proud of his reaction to the hard hit Jalen Hurts took from Chicago Bears linebacker D'Marco Jackson in the second quarter on Monday night.
articles.body:
Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni is not proud of his reaction to the hard hit Jalen Hurts took from Chicago Bears linebacker D'Marco Jackson in the second quarter on Monday night.

Speaking to reporters after the Eagles' 27-7 loss, Sirianni expressed "remorse" for yelling at Jackson after the play.

"Obviously, you want to always fight for your players, and protect your players. I always come away when I have a moment like that with remorse of, 'Man, I shouldn't have let my emotions get the best of me,'" Sirianni said.

Player gets drug tested after viral clip

The play saw Hurts scramble and run toward the sideline trying to pick up a first down. As he was stepping out of bounds, Jackson hit him hard in the shoulder area and knocked him off his feet.

Sirianni was seen on the sideline appearing to yell expletives in Jackson's direction after the play.

Jackson was flagged for unnecessary roughness, but there were offsetting penalties due to a holding call against Lane Johnson. The officials directed Hurts off the field to be evaluated for a concussion.

Hurts cleared concussion protocol, but the drive ended with Andy Dalton throwing an interception to Bears safety Dillon Thieneman in the end zone to keep Chicago up 7-0 midway through the second quarter.

The Eagles suffered their first loss of the season on Monday night. Their seven points was their fewest in a game since Week 12 of the 2021 season against the New York Giants, which was Sirianni's first year as head coach.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers backs $199.99-a-year platform built to connect brands with pro athletes
articles.summary: Last year, Aaron Rodgers was still focused on life inside the NFL, but his business interests were already moving in a different direction.
articles.body: Last year, Aaron Rodgers was still focused on life inside the NFL, but his business interests were already moving in a different direction. The Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback is now backing a startup designed to change how companies, charities and sponsors find professional athletes. AthleteAgent.com, which launched as a rebrand of Online Sports Database, is positioning itself as a central hub for athlete and agent information, with Rodgers among its original founders and a seven-figure investment in the company.Aaron Rodgers backs AthleteAgent.comThe idea behind AthleteAgent.com began with actor and producer Ryan Rottman in 2021. He saw a clear difference between the way actors and athletes could be discovered online. His experience with IMDb showed him how useful verified representation details could be when producers wanted to make contact quickly.Rottman eventually brought the concept to Rodgers, who became an early supporter. The platform now offers information on more than 4,000 athletes and 2,000 agents. Profiles can include representation, endorsements, contract information and charitable work.Rodgers is not the only major name supporting the venture. Sports agent Scott Boras and several investment firms are also involved. The company declined to disclose the quarterback's precise investment but confirmed that it was worth seven figures.For Rodgers, the project also creates a connection between his playing career and the wider sports business world.AthleteAgent.com targets athlete accessAthleteAgent.com operates through a subscription model, charging $29.99 a month or $199.99 a year for full database access. Its goal is to make outreach more direct while helping organisations avoid contacting the wrong representative.CEO Sean O'Brien said the company is on track to generate six-figure revenue and positive cash flow during the year. The business also plans to expand beyond active athletes by adding team executives, front office contacts and retired players.Rottman believes the platform can give more athletes opportunities beyond the biggest names in professional sports.“Aaron likes to say we’re building this not for the 1% of athletes, but for the other 99% — to help generate revenue, get their stories out there, find endorsement deals, support their charities. That’s how it came to fruition,” Rottman said.The company says agents can also benefit because they can respond to endorsement opportunities without paying a commission to the platform.O'Brien highlighted how the database can help brands identify the right business contact rather than simply approaching an athlete's most famous representative.The wider ambition is clear. articles.title: New NFL Rumors on Giants' J.J. McCarthy Evaluation Before 2024 Draft, Concerns About QB
articles.summary: On the heels of the New York Giants acquiring quarterback J.J. McCarthy in a trade with the Minnesota Vikings on Monday, reported details have emerged regarding how the Giants viewed McCarthy leading up to the 2024 NFL draft.
articles.body:
On the heels of the New York Giants acquiring quarterback J.J. McCarthy in a trade with the Minnesota Vikings on Monday, reported details have emerged regarding how the Giants viewed McCarthy leading up to the 2024 NFL draft.

According to Paul Schwartz of the New York Post , the Giants scouted McCarthy prior to the 2024 NFL draft, and it is believed that they had a second-round grade on him.

Harbaugh Reveals Giants QB1 After McCarthy Trade

One of the factors in the Giants not viewing McCarthy as a first-rounder is that they reportedly "had reservations about his mental makeup and how he would fare playing in the fishbowl of the New York/New Jersey market."

With Jaxson Dart out for the remainder of the regular season due to a knee injury, the Giants got aggressive this week in an effort to add depth to their quarterback room.

They gave up only a 2027 fifth-round draft pick for McCarthy, who was the No. 10 overall selection in the 2024 NFL draft.

Giants head coach John Harbaugh told reporters that veteran quarterback Jameis Winston will remain the starter, but McCarthy gives them another option should Winston struggle or get injured.

While Joe Schoen was the Giants' general manager in 2024 and remains in that role currently, Harbaugh's arrival is the biggest difference when it comes to the organization's chain of command.

It may not be a coincidence that the Giants' acquisition of McCarthy comes amid Harbaugh having a significant link to the young signal-caller.

During McCarthy's collegiate playing days at Michigan, his head coach was current Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh, who is John Harbaugh's brother.

With McCarthy at the helm, Michigan went undefeated and won the national championship in 2023.

That level of success has eluded McCarthy thus far in the NFL, as he failed to establish himself as the long-term starter in Minnesota.

After missing his entire rookie season due to a knee injury, McCarthy made 10 starts for the Vikings last season.

He did manage a 6-4 record, but his statistical output left plenty to be desired, as he completed 57.6 percent of his passes for 1,632 yards, 11 touchdowns and 12 interceptions, while also rushing for 181 yards and four scores.

The Vikings signed veteran quarterback Kyler Murray during the offseason as competition, and it didn't take long into training camp for Murray to be named the starter.

When McCarthy ended up third on the depth chart behind both Murray and Carson Wentz, the writing seemed to be on the wall regarding McCarthy's fate in Minnesota.

Now he has new surroundings, and although the Giants were reportedly once concerned about how McCarthy's psyche would handle such a huge media market, the fact that he doesn't have to be immediately thrust into a starting role could potentially help him acclimate.

articles.title: Week 4 Fantasy Football Rankings, Top Players, Sleepers and Positional Guide
articles.summary: The 2026 NFL season continues to turn fantasy football into a rocky roller coaster of a ride. That trend continues in Week 3, as fans witnessed more big upsets, stunning finishes, impressive 2026 debuts and, unfortunately, more significant injuries.
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL season continues to turn fantasy football into a rocky roller coaster of a ride. That trend continues in Week 3, as fans witnessed more big upsets, stunning finishes, impressive 2026 debuts and, unfortunately, more significant injuries.

The uncertainty makes it difficult to sort through the Week 4 fantasy landscape this early in the week. Fortunately, managers still have another week before byes also factor into the equation.

However, the Indianapolis Colts and Washington Commanders will play an international game on Sunday morning, so don't forget to set those lineups early.

Here, you'll find early point-per-reception (PPR) rankings for Week 4, along with a few sleepers to consider targeting on the waiver wire.

Though he was unable to get the New York Jets a win in Week 3, Geno Smith did take advantage of a suspect Detroit Lions defense. In a back-and-forth battle that saw the Lions pull away late, Smith threw for 321 yards and three touchdowns.

This week, Smith and the Jets will take on a Chicago Bears that showed on Monday it can put up points without Caleb Williams. With Breece Hall battling a thigh injury, the Jets will likely call on Smith early and often. His ceiling is probably limited, but Smith is a serviceable option for managers who have lost Jaxson Dart, Jayden Daniels, or Caleb Williams to injury.

Smith is rostered in only 10 percent of fantasy leagues.

Christian McCaffrey, San Francisco 49ers

Sleeper: Brian Robinson Jr., RB, Atlanta Falcons

Running backs have been a scarce commodity this season, and with byes on the not-too-distant horizon, it's worth scooping up a matchup-based flex option like Brian Robinson Jr.

Brian Robinson is obviously the Atlanta Falcons' No. 2 back behind Bijan Robinson. However, he has reached 50 scrimmage yards in consecutive weeks with a pair of receptions in Week 2 and a touchdown in Week 3.

This week, Robinson will face a New Orleans Saints defense that has surrendered an average of 24.2 fantasy points to opposing backfields. He's rostered in just 31 percent of fantasy leagues.

Sleeper: Keenan Allen, WR, Indianapolis Colts

The Colts recently placed standout receiver Alec Pierce on injured reserve with a heel issue. With Pierce out of the lineup on Sunday, Keenan Allen emerged as a go-to target and finished with six catches for 63 yards and a touchdown on nine targets.

Pierce will be out at least another three weeks, so Allen should at least carry some short-term value. This week, he'll face the Commanders in London, a situation that can be exploited. Washington has surrendered an average of 39 fantasy points to opposing receiver groups so far this season.

Allen is rostered in only 21 percent of fantasy leagues.

Preseason Contenders in Desperation Mode

Sleeper: T.J. Hockenson, TE, Minnesota Vikings

Minnesota Vikings receiver Justin Jefferson suffered an ankle injury on Sunday and did not return to the game. While that doesn't guarantee that he'll miss Week 4, Minnesota will undoubtedly exercise caution approaching a matchup with the winless Miami Dolphins.

This gives tight end T.J. Hockenson some legitimate sleeper value for, really, the first time this season. He did catch a touchdown pass in Week 1, but he hasn't topped three receptions or reached 30 receiving yards in a game since. A lot will hinge on Jefferson's status, but Hockenson is worth adding in deeper leagues this week.
