articles.title: 5 NFL Coordinators and Coaches Who Should Already be on the Hot Seat After Week 3
articles.summary: There are several head coaches and coordinators whose seats are getting rather warm less than a month into the 2026 NFL season.
articles.body:
There are several head coaches and coordinators whose seats are getting rather warm less than a month into the 2026 NFL season.

Although these coaches may have come into the new campaign in a seemingly stable position, they're already on shaky ground following some disappointing early results.

Week 3 represented a new low for several teams that have slumped out of the gate. Five teams remain winless through three games and many others have mustered just a single victory in that span. There's still an opportunity for each of these squads to turn things around, but time is quickly running out.

If these franchises don't get back on track and string together some wins in the next few weeks, major changes will be inevitable. Although most clubs won't take the nuclear option of dismissing key staff in the initial months of a trying season, drastic measures such as a shift in play-calling duties aren't far off.

With that in mind, let's highlight five coaches who are firmly on the hot seat after Week 3.

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have been a middling team for much of the Todd Bowles era. Rather than steadily improve with the head coach at the wheel, the Bucs have backslid following the three consecutive playoff appearances that opened his tenure.

After an 8-9 campaign last year resulted in the franchise's first missed postseason berth since 2019, Bowles had to be feeling pressure to get Tampa back on track in 2026. Losing three consecutive games to open the season hasn't done anything to help Bowles' job security and there's now a chance he becomes the first coach to be fired this year.

No Bucs coach has survived two consecutive losing seasons since the Glazer family purchased the franchise in 1995. While ownership has waited until the conclusion of a second down year to fire the likes of Greg Schiano, Lovie Smith and Dirk Koetter, this utterly dismal start could force a change prior to the offseason.

Things are looking especially bleak in Tampa now that star quarterback Baker Mayfield—the recipient of a blockbuster contract extension just before the 2026 season kicked off—is set to miss upwards of a month or more with a dislocated thumb on his right throwing hand. The Bucs now must turn to undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels to run a passing offense that already ranked in the bottom quarter of the league with Mayfield under center.

While the Mayfield injury is unfortunate, the Bucs' struggles aren't new. The team opened 2025 on a 6-2 tear before fumbling away a fifth consecutive NFC South crown with a 2-7 finish. Bowles made a litany of staffing adjustments following the 8-9 season, including dismissing the team's offensive and special teams coordinators in addition to several key positional coaches.

Those changes clearly haven't worked, leaving Bowles as the final domino left to fall. His fate is all but sealed, so expect a regime change in Tampa barring a miraculous winning streak over the next few months.

The Tennessee Titans came into the 2026 NFL season with real potential to follow in the footsteps of the New England Patriots, becoming the latest team to orchestrate a worst-to-first turnaround engineered by a promising second-year quarterback and new coaching staff.

After an embarrassing 0-3 start, the Robert Saleh-led Titans are now facing an uphill battle to even post a winning season, let alone punch a playoff ticket after a half-decade absence or make a Super Bowl appearance for the first time since the 1999 campaign.

The main catalyst behind Tennessee's shortcomings has been offensive coordinator Brian Daboll's inability to develop 2025 No. 1 overall pick Cam Ward.

Although the Titans largely struggled during his rookie campaign, Ward flashed the potential to be a franchise quarterback and appeared poised to make a significant Year 2 leap.

Unfortunately for the Titans, Ward has seemingly regressed rather than improve over the first three games of 2026. He's completed just 62.5 percent of his throws for a meager 504 yards and two touchdowns in that span.

While the 2025 No. 1 overall pick has only turned the ball over once and taken just five sacks after leading the league with 55 last year, he's failed to make the type of impact expected from a franchise-caliber quarterback.

With Tennessee ranking No. 30 in both scoring and passing offense while putting up just 37 points across three contests—the third-fewest in the league—there is cause for genuine concern regarding Saleh's selection of Daboll as his offensive coordinator.

Daboll came to the Music City following a rough tenure with the New York Giants, putting together just one winning season during his four years at the reins. The offense was largely inconsistent during that span, problems that are now reflecting far worse on Daboll than the players he had tasked with running his system.

While Daboll will have a few more opportunities to figure things out—starting in Week 4 when the Titans take on a middling Baltimore Ravens defense—he can't expect to remain with the franchise long if he doesn't get far better results from his offense over the next few weeks.

The Los Angeles Chargers' 0-3 start is one the most surprising storylines of the 2026 NFL season.

While there are glaring issues with offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel for his inability to spark a talent-laden unit and defensive coordinator Chris O'Leary's failure to achieve the same strong results that predecessor Jesse Minter received from this group, head coach Jim Harbaugh deserves the lion's share of blame for the Chargers' struggles.

Harbaugh didn't properly prepare his team for the new season. While injuries were a huge component of the team's late-season skid in 2025—as well as its second consecutive playoff crash-out under the head coach—there are no such excuses this time around.

The Bolts were soundly beaten by two inferior opponents in the Arizona Cardinals and Las Vegas Raiders to open the year, setting up a must-win Week 3 showdown with the Buffalo Bills.

Rather than prove those two losses were flukes and that the Chargers can hang with the class of the AFC, L.A. could not close out a Bills team that turned the ball over five times and tallied a season-low 24 points.

With the Chargers now ranking in the bottom half of the league in every major offensive category besides rushing (including No. 29 in scoring offense), every major defensive category and tied for the third-most giveaways in football, it's impossible not to place Harbaugh on the hot seat.

While Harbaugh has gotten consistently strong results at every stop of his career and helped a listless Chargers squad reach the playoffs in each of his first two seasons, that streak is in serious jeopardy due to this abysmal start.

The Bolts won't find it any easier to turn things around over the next couple months. This stretch includes showdowns with the Seattle Seahawks, Denver Broncos and Kansas City Chiefs leading up to a Week 7 bye, as well as a date with the in-town rival Los Angeles Rams coming out of it.

If L.A. stumbles through this portion of the schedule, the team will be out of the running and Harbaugh will be forced to make sweeping changes to his staff well before things get any easier in the back half of the campaign.

Preseason Contenders in Desperation Mode

The Green Bay Packers have been one of the league's more consistent teams during the Matt LaFleur era, but they've yet to make a leap into serious Super Bowl contention.

Hopes for the club to level up in 2026 have rapidly diminished after the team limped out to a 1-2 start during what was arguably the easiest three-game stretch on their entire schedule.

Green Bay hasn't looked right since the fourth quarter of the opener against the rival Minnesota Vikings, a contest in which the Packers were outscored 22-0 in the fourth quarter and lost by a 39-22 margin despite leading for much of the game. They rebounded to knock off the lowly New York Jets in overtime, but fell flat once again against a previously winless Atlanta Falcons opponent in a prime-time Thursday Night Football contest.

LaFleur called the Atlanta loss "humbling" and described it as a "butt-whooping," admitting he needs to work with his team to "try to figure out what we do well, because right now, I don't know what we're doing well offensively."

The slow start to the 2026 season follows Green Bay's collapse in the Wild Card Round of the playoffs. The Packers blew a 21-3 lead to their bitter NFC North rival, the Chicago Bears, the latest in an increasingly disappointing string of postseason shortcomings under LaFleur.

While LaFleur has had just one losing season since taking the reins in 2019, he hasn't made it back to the NFC Championship Game since Aaron Rodgers' last MVP season in 2020 and has only advanced past the Wild Card Round once since Jordan Love assumed the starting quarterback role on a full-time basis in 2023.

Although he's earned a longer leash than most coaches for his consistent winning ways, LaFleur will be forced to make some major adjustments if the Packers continue to slide over the next few weeks.

If he can't turn the ship around, there will be serious discussions about his future in Titletown.

Defensive woes were the main culprit behind the Dallas Cowboys' disappointing 7-9-1 finish last year, a glaring issue that led head coach Brian Schottenheimer to relieve Matt Eberflus of his defensive coordinator post.

Christian Parker, Eberflus' replacement for 2026, has arguably done less with more after the Cowboys spent the offseason reinforcing multiple areas of weakness across their defensive lineup.

Those pricey investments, which included expending five of seven draft picks on defensive prospects (including first-rounders Caleb Downs and Malachi Lawrence) and adding impact veterans such as Rashan Gary, Von Miller and Quinnen Williams, haven't paid off. The Cowboys currently rank No. 31 in rushing defense, No. 30 in total defense and No. 25 in scoring defense.

Although the Cowboys are dealing with several notable injuries, the team's inability to put pressure on opposing signal-callers (Dallas has just two sacks on the year, the third-fewest in football) and create turnovers (also tied for the third-fewest with two) is inexcusable. Even the passing defense, which rates a more respectable No. 15, has severely let the club down.

While a series of errors allowed the Baltimore Ravens to set up a walk-off field goal in Week 3, Parker's decision to play man-to-man defense on the penultimate snap was among the most consequential. Zay Flowers then beat Dallas' secondary for a 27-yard gain, putting the Ravens in position to walk it off.

The humiliating defeat dropped the Cowboys to 1-2 and has put them in danger of missing the playoffs for the third consecutive year. The team is squandering another solid offensive season with inept defensive play and must figure things out before it's too late.

Parker will get another chance to fix things when the Cowboys face the winless Houston Texans in Week 4. If he can't get the defense to shut down a toothless foe that rates in the bottom quarter of the NFL in both rushing offense and scoring, Schottenheimer has to give serious consideration to changing his defensive play-caller.

articles.title: Cowboys' Jerry Jones Talks Errors in Stunning Loss to Ravens, 'No Explanation You're Satisfied With'
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones is still trying to process the end-of-game sequence that led to his team's 34-31 loss to the Baltimore Ravens in Rio de Janeiro on Sunday.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones is still trying to process the end-of-game sequence that led to his team's 34-31 loss to the Baltimore Ravens in Rio de Janeiro on Sunday.

During his Tuesday appearance on 105.3 The Fan's Shan & RJ show, Jones explained there's "no explanation you're satisfied with" while talking about Dak Prescott's third-down throwaway to set up a game-tying field goal rather than attempt to go for the win in that situation.

Cowboys HC gives himself an F after loss to Ravens

There were multiple issues with Dallas' late-game execution and time management in the game.

Even before Prescott's decision to throw the ball away on third down from the Ravens' five-yard line, the Cowboys had a first-and-goal from the two with 23 seconds remaining.

The sequence from there went incomplete pass, false start and a two-yard run from Prescott that forced Dallas to take its final timeout to stop the clock.

Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer told reporters after the game that Prescott was coached to throw the ball away on that third down, even though it appeared George Pickens had enough separation to potentially catch a go-ahead touchdown if the ball had been thrown toward him instead of far over his head.

Following Brandon Aubrey's game-tying field goal, the Cowboys helped out Baltimore by having the ensuing kickoff go into the end zone for a touchback to keep seven seconds on the clock.

If the Cowboys had kicked the ball short of the end zone, the Ravens' return would have at least run enough time off the clock that they would have had to attempt a Hail Mary.

The argument against that strategy would be Baltimore could potentially return the kickoff for a game-winning touchdown, but the odds of that happening are significantly lower than letting the Ravens complete a pass, get a timeout and attempt a field goal.

That wound up being exactly what happened. Lamar Jackson connected with Zay Flowers for a 27-yard gain, allowing Tyler Loop to kick the game-winning 56-yard-field goal.

Per ESPN's Benjamin Solak , this game marked the first time in the Super Bowl era both teams kicked a field goal in the last 10 seconds of the fourth quarter.

The loss dropped Dallas' record to 1-2 this season with both losses coming by a combined 11 points. The Cowboys will look to get back to the .500 mark on Sunday against the Houston Texans at Reliant Stadium.

articles.title: Jerry Jones Hints at Ongoing Cowboys Trade Talks amid Joey Porter Jr., Steelers Rumors
articles.summary: After falling to 1-2 following Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Baltimore Ravens in the NFL Rio Game, the Dallas Cowboys could see some changes soon.
articles.body:
After falling to 1-2 following Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Baltimore Ravens in the NFL Rio Game, the Dallas Cowboys could see some changes soon.

During his weekly radio appearance on 105.3 The Fan, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said there are active "conversations going on" about potentially upgrading the team's roster through the trade market. While Jones chose not to comment on Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. to avoid tampering, it's safe to say the 26-year-old is near the top of Dallas' target list.

ESPN's Adam Schefter recently reported that the Cowboys are among "a handful of teams" that have "begun making inquiries about the availability" of Porter, who has missed the first three games of the 2026 season while recovering from a back injury. Sources told Schefter that the Steelers "would be willing to listen to trade offers for Porter," but they "would want a strong compensation package if they were to deal the fourth-year star."

Preseason Contenders in Desperation Mode

Dallas has focused on improving its defense over the last year, acquiring defensive linemen Quinnen Williams, Rashan Gary and Kenny Clark in trades and using its two 2026 first-round draft picks to select safety Caleb Downs and linebacker Malachi Lawrence.

Despite the defensive overhaul, the Cowboys are still searching for answers. Through the first three weeks of the 2026 campaign, the team ranks 30th in the NFL with 387.0 yards allowed per game.

It sounds like Jones is willing to continue being aggressive in finding trades to help the Cowboys improve. Dallas will try to get back on track when it faces the Houston Texans (0-3) in Week 4.

articles.title: “We did everything together you know": How Travis Kelce's childhood rival became family and stayed close through his journey from Cleveland to NFL fame
articles.summary: Travis Kelce has spent more than a decade in the NFL spotlight, but some of the people closest to him knew him long before the Chiefs star became a
articles.body: Travis Kelce has spent more than a decade in the NFL spotlight, but some of the people closest to him knew him long before the Chiefs star became a household name. Aric Jones is one of them. The two met as young children in Cleveland Heights and grew up playing sports together, competing for starting spots and eventually becoming part of the same close-knit circle. Their friendship survived high school, college, Kelce’s move to Kansas City and his rise to NFL stardom.How Travis Kelce and Aric Jones went from childhood competitors to familyKelce and Jones first met in 1995 at the Cleveland Heights Recreation Center while playing youth hockey. Jones has described those early years as the foundation of a friendship that grew through several sports. They played hockey, attended basketball camps and eventually became teammates and competitors in football.Their friendship also had a competitive side. In high school, Kelce was the starting quarterback while Jones served as the backup quarterback and starting safety. Kelce wore No. 1 and Jones wore No. 2, and both earned all-league recognition.Jones explained the dynamic during a 2023 interview with Ideastream Public Media.“He was QB one, I was QB two,” Jones said. “I was the starting safety on defense. He was starting quarterback. He wore number one. I wore number two. We were both all-league at the same time. We did everything together, you know what I mean?”The relationship extended beyond the field. Their families also became close, with Jones describing Travis’ parents, Ed and Donna Kelce, as people who remain like family to him. Donna was around the team during their high school years, making food for the players before games.Jones later recalled just how much of his teenage life included Kelce. In a 2024 interview with PEOPLE, he said, “I went to my first house party with Travis. I got in my first car accident with Travis. He was there for so much of my, honestly, just teenage-ness.”Sports also continued to connect them after high school. When they went to different colleges, they still made the effort to watch each other play. Jones said Kelce would drive hours to see him, while he returned the support.That bond continued when Kelce entered the NFL. The Chiefs selected him in the third round of the 2013 NFL Draft, and Jones was finishing school at Tennessee State the following year. Instead of letting distance change their friendship, Kelce invited Jones to move into his Kansas City home.How Travis Kelce brought his childhood friend into his Kansas City lifeJones was initially unsure about accepting the invitation. In Vanity Fair’s July/August 2023 issue, he recalled asking Kelce if he was certain about the arrangement because he did not want to become a burden.Kelce responded by sending him a picture of a bedroom. “Here’s your room. It’s waiting for you,” Kelce told him, according to Jones’ account in Vanity Fair.Jones lived with Kelce for two years. By then, the friendship had moved well beyond childhood sports. Kelce’s NFL career was taking off, but Jones remained part of the group that knew him before the fame.That circle later became a regular part of Kelce’s football life. Jones has been part of the Kelce family suite since 2016 and became known as the group’s “party captain.” He was also there for major moments, including Kelce’s Super Bowl appearances. Ideastream documented Jones attending the 2020 Super Bowl with Kelce’s Cleveland Heights friends and joining the Kelce family for the 2021 game.“Still, to this day, as a group of friends, we all have a saying to each other: do your job, and everybody is a star in their own role,” Jones told PEOPLE in 2024.He also offered a simple description of the role their friendship plays around Kelce’s enormous public profile.“Travis is the car, and everybody sees the Bentley, and they see the Ferrari, but are you popping the hood? ’Cause we’re the engine,” Jones said.Away from football, their friendship still resembles the Cleveland Heights days. Jones said the group jokes around, talks trash, argues about football and revisits old memories like they are back at their high school lunch table. He also recalled spending Thanksgiving 2023 with Kelce and friends, eating KFC and watching movies.Their friendship has also remained connected to their hometown. Jones created the lifestyle brand Homebred, which grew out of his Cleveland Heights roots, and Kelce has supported the brand by wearing its gear. In 2024, Jones told KCUR that Kelce had worn Homebred clothing at press conferences, during the Super Bowl and privately.Jones remains part of the close circle surrounding Kelce. articles.title: The NFL returns to the UK more committed than ever to international growth after Rio and Melbourne games - but is a European team possible?
articles.summary: The NFL will play three games in London across the next month as part of a record nine international games in the 2026 season, having already made debuts in Melbourne, Australia and Rio de Janeiro, Brazil; Sky Sports' Neil Reynolds explores the NFL's future overseas in his weekly column
articles.body:
We'll see the Indianapolis Colts take on the Washington Commanders at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Sunday and the following week we will welcome back the Jacksonville Jaguars as they clash with the Philadelphia Eagles at the same venue.

The trio of games will end at Wembley Stadium on October 18 with the Jags taking on their division rivals in the AFC South in the Houston Texans.

The NFL continues its commitment to the UK but it's clear they are looking more globally than ever before. By the end of this 2026 season we will have seen nine regular season games played internationally and the NFL is growing braver.

I think London played a big part in that as well by proving time and time again how you can get teams in, get them practising efficiently, get them playing the game and then get them out.

That blueprint has now been taken quite literally to the other side of the world. So this season we'll see firsts with games already played in Australia and in Rio de Janeiro in Brazil. We'll also see a first this year with a game in Paris, France towards the end of October.

So this NFL train is not slowing down. In fact it's only going to gather pace. I think we'll see 10 games played next season and I don't think we're very far away from seeing 16 being played internationally every year.

That of course will come once the league negotiates any new deal with the Players Association that takes the regular season up to 18 games from its current 17 right now. So at first glance the league is intent on continuing with its Formula 1 approach. Different teams playing in different markets, growing the fanbase around the entire world and I understand why.

I've spoken to NFL commissioner Roger Goodell about this in the past and he's told me that if we play in just one or two markets you only grow the fanbase in one or two markets. If you can play in 10, 11, 12 markets around the world then you're growing significantly in a number of different countries, so it certainly looks like that's the plan, but we still hear this talk of international franchises, potentially even a European division and the commissioner himself alluded to that this summer when in Germany.

I think the reason for that is that the NFL just doesn't want to lose momentum. So they are keeping an open mind. Yes at the moment it's the Formula 1 approach but if it works well enough in enough countries then does it become something else? Does it become something more substantial in London? Do we have a European division with a team in London, one in Germany, one in Spain, one in France?

When you look at it you can see the groundwork being laid for that.

I think if I were a betting man I wouldn't necessarily know which way to go. I've seen very early on a lot of talk about a franchise, especially in London, then that went away to a degree and we looked at this Formula 1 approach of different teams in different countries.

But now the commissioner has put the franchise discussion back on the table which to me suggests the league is just focusing at the moment on continuing to grow fan numbers, continuing to grow interest, finding new fans and players through flag football and seeing where it goes in the future.

I don't think they're committed to one path or the other and it won't hurt that we're using the Formula 1 approach now and then pivot to something else later.

I tell you one thing, the commitment has never been greater among NFL owners and commissioner Roger Goodell to grow the game internationally.

It is one of the biggest things the NFL will be working on now and for many years to come and for us as fans of the game internationally that can only be good news for us.

articles.title: Bears Backup QB Case Keenum Celebrates Upset Win Over Eagles with Daughter in Sweet Postgame Scene
articles.summary: The signal-caller had a stellar night, completing 24 of 34 passes for 247 yards and two touchdowns in the Bears’ 27-7 win over the Eagles
articles.body:
Case Keenum celebrated with his daughter after the Bears -Eagles game on Monday Night Football

The backup quarterback led Bears to a 27-7 win over the Eagles

Keenum was playing his first NFL game after more than 1,000 days

It was a night to remember for Case Keenum — and his daughter, Cadence!

On Monday, Sept. 28, the third-string Chicago Bears quarterback, 38, started in his first NFL game after more than 1,000 days.

And he tore the proverbial roof off Soldier Field in his performance, after being inserted into the lineup in the wake of Caleb Williams' hamstring injury .

When the dust cleared in the Bears' 27-7 win over the Philadelphia Eagles , Keenum's presence was required on ESPN, and Cadence happily joined him at the desk.

"It was so much fun," Case told Scott Van Pelt. "I'm going to remember this night forever. This is incredible."

For Keenum — a 15-year NFL veteran who has played with the Texans , Rams , Vikings, Broncos , Commanders (then Redskins), Browns and Bills — experience played a role in his stellar performance.

The Texas native completed 24 of 34 attempts for 247 yards and two touchdowns en route to the victory.

But playing in front of his family, including his parents and in-laws , was a moment he'll most cherish.

"I thought of them a lot on the sidelines," Keenum told Van Pelt. "To have my wife, Kimberly, and Kyler and Cadence to be able to [say], hey they're watching their dad out there play. And it was so much fun."

The signal-caller earned a game ball from head coach Ben Johnson and gave a rousing, emotional speech in the locker room after the game.

"Man I love you guys, it's a special night, this was taken from me many times," Keenum said. "To have my family, my kids watching, and get to do it with this family right here."

He added, "I may not be a Cowboy but this isn't my first f---ing rodeo!"

articles.title: Georgia Bulldogs leading the way for the NFL's biggest surprise
articles.summary: Former Georgia Bulldogs tight end Brock Bowers and linebacker Nakobe Dean helped the Raiders to a shocking 3-0 start.
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders have started 3-0 and are the NFL's biggest surprise to start the season after picking No. 1 in the 2026 NFL draft. The Raiders kept their winning streak going with a comeback 35-27 victory over the New Orleans Saints . Two former Georgia Bulldogs paved the way: tight end Brock Bowers and linebacker Nakobe Dean .

Bowers made his season debut after missing the first two games of the season with a meniscus injury. The two-time Pro Bowl tight end picked up right where he left off, nabbing 10 receptions for 110 yards and a touchdown. His touchdown came with 6:22 left to go when the Raiders were up 28-27.

Dean might've made more of an impact. The former Butkus Award-winning linebacker signed with the Raiders in free agency, and he's paid off immediately. So far, he has 27 tackles, three tackles for loss, 1.5 sacks, and three forced fumbles. He's forced a fumble in every game.

Against the Saints, Dean forced a fumble from Juwan Johnson on the Saints' final drive down 35-27, and it was recovered by Eric Stokes , who is also a former Georgia Bulldog.

The Raiders are one of four teams with at least five Georgia Bulldogs on their roster. Along with Bowers, Dean, and Stokes, they have defensive end Azeez Ojulari and linebacker Quay Walker . The Raiders join the Vikings (five), Bengals (five) and Eagles (six) in that regard. All four of these teams have winning records and were undefeated coming into Week 3, with the Raiders and Vikings still undefeated after Week 3.

Dean and Bowers are two of the most legendary Georgia players in school history. When Dean was at Georgia, he earned 168 tackles, 14.5 tackles for loss, 7.5 sacks, eight pass breakups, two interceptions, three forced fumbles, and a fumble-return touchdown. Dean earned the 2021 Butkus Award and a unanimous All-American selection for garnering 72 tackles, 10.5 TFLs, six sacks, six PBUs, two interceptions, two forced fumbles, and a scoop-and-score against Florida. He also helped Georgia win a national championship in 2021.

Bowers was legendary throughout his career. Among all Georgia Bulldogs in history, he ranks No. 3 in receptions (175), No. 5 in yards (2,538), and No. 2 in touchdowns (26). He was an All-SEC team member every year of his three-year tenure with Georgia (2021-23), a second-team All-American in 2021, a first-team All-American in 2022, and a unanimous All-American in 2023. He won the John Mackey Award in 2022 and 2023, the only tight end to ever win the award twice. Oh yeah, and he also helped the Bulldogs win two national championships.

articles.title: Odell Beckham Jr. Released by Giants, Had 0 Catches in 3 Games After Reunion
articles.summary: Odell Beckham Jr.'s second stint with the New York Giants has come to an end after three games.
articles.body:
Odell Beckham Jr.'s second stint with the New York Giants has come to an end after three games.

Beckham was released by the Giants after receiving just one target with no catches through the first three weeks of the 2026 season.

NFL Network's Mike Garafolo and Ian Rapoport first reported the news.

NFL insider Jordan Schultz added the decision was mutual from both parties with Beckham hoping to land with a team that can better utilize his talent.

That news appeared to catch Giants linebacker Kayvon Thibodeaux by surprise:

Beckham signed with the Giants on June 1, reuniting with the franchise that originally drafted him in 2014. It also marked his return to the NFL after sitting out the 2025 season.

The last time Beckham appeared in an NFL game was in Week 14 of the 2024 season with the Miami Dolphins. He was released a few days after that.

New York added Beckham in part as insurance for Malik Nabers, who was recovering from a torn ACL suffered early in the 2025 season. He performed well in the preseason with seven receptions for 76 yards in three games.

The Giants included Beckham on their 53-man roster after final cuts on Aug. 30. He was part of a receiver room that included Nabers, Malachi Fields, Darnell Mooney and Darius Slayton.

Nabers and Fields have been the two starting receivers for the Giants through the first three weeks. Mooney ranks third on the team in receiving yards so far, behind Isaiah Likely and Nabers.

Beckham has only played 20 offensive snaps through the first three games. He got his first target in Sunday's win over the Tennessee Titans.

If this does mark the end of Beckham's time with the Giants, his 5,476 receiving yards rank as the second-most in franchise history. His 88.3 yards per game is the most for a Giants player.

articles.title: Bears vs. Packers Time Changed on Week 5 of 2026 NFL Schedule amid Caleb Williams Injury
articles.summary: This season's Chicago Bears at Green Bay Packers matchup was scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET on Sunday, Oct. 11, but that game has now been moved to 1 p.m.
articles.body:
This season's Chicago Bears at Green Bay Packers matchup was scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET on Sunday, Oct. 11, but that game has now been moved to 1 p.m.

Jonathan Jones of The Athletic provided more information.

Folks can make educated guesses why the Bears and Packers were flexed out of Fox's featured national game of the week, despite forming the league's most storied and heated rivalry.

For starters, Bears quarterback Caleb Williams, who is dealing with a Grade 2 hamstring injury, has a reported three to four-week injury timeline dating back to Sept. 20, when he initially suffered the ailment in a 9-3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings. He appears likely to miss this game.

In addition, the 1-2 Packers have not started the season well and are coming off an ugly 35-14 home loss to the previously winless Atlanta Falcons. Green Bay lost 39-22 to Minnesota to start the season and squeaked by the New York Jets, 20-17 in overtime, in Week 2.

The 2-1 Bears have done their part as a competitive and watchable team. They've enjoyed a mostly strong start to the season, beginning the 2026 campaign with a 59-37 win over the Carolina Panthers.

The defensive rock fight with the Minnesota Vikings followed, but then third-string quarterback Case Keenum enjoyed a phenomenal performance (247 passing yards, two passing touchdowns, one rushing score) in a 27-7 win over the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday evening.

Still, given the Packers' early performance and a star in Williams' absence, one can surmise that the undefeated San Francisco 49ers taking on the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks offers more appeal to NFL fans right now, which is why it moved to FOX's America's Game of the Week.

San Francisco is one of the NFL's five remaining undefeated teams. Brock Purdy is an early NFL MVP candidate, and the 49ers have scored the second-most points in football (98).

The 2-1 Seahawks just lost a tough 33-31 road game to the previously winless Washington Commanders, but they are loaded with talent from last year's Super Bowl team and should still be strong playoff contenders this season.

articles.title: Jerry Jones on late-game Cowboys meltdown in loss to Ravens: 'There is no explanation that you're satisfied with'
articles.summary: Jones was candid about Sunday's mistakes that led to Baltimore's win in regulation. But he wasn't ready to join Cowboys fans with a pitchfork for Brian Schot...
articles.body:
Dallas is a disappointing 1-2 and fresh off one of the wildest meltdowns of this or any NFL season in a loss to the Baltimore Ravens . This makes Jerry Jones' weekly radio hit a must-listen.

Jones, as he does every week during the season, joined 105.3 The Fan on Tuesday to talk Dallas Cowboys football. He spoke candidly about the late-game breakdown that allowed the Ravens to kick a walk-off, 56-yard field goal and secure a 34-31 win over his Cowboys Sunday . But he stopped short of joining Cowboys fans in ramping up the pressure on head coach Brian Schottenheimer's job.

'There is no explanation you're satisfied with'

Most notably, Jones addressed head coach Brian Schottenheimer's explanation for the bizarre third-down play on offense in which Dak Prescott immediately threw the ball away after the snap rather than target an open George Pickens in the end zone.

"There is no explanation you're satisfied with," Jones said. "None. Let's be sure that we all understand that. They don't have one that they're satisfied with. "We made mistakes during that time. There's no question about it. So there is no explanation. But there's an evaluation of how not to make the same mistakes again, which is what you should be doing."

"There is no explanation you're satisfied with," Jones said. "None. Let's be sure that we all understand that. They don't have one that they're satisfied with.

"We made mistakes during that time. There's no question about it. So there is no explanation. But there's an evaluation of how not to make the same mistakes again, which is what you should be doing."

Jones called for accountability, but calm

This was the theme of Jones' radio hit. He didn't gloss over the late-game mistakes that have sparked wave of criticism in Dallas of Schottenheimer, who is in his second season as the Cowboys' head coach.

But Jones didn't join the fanbase with a pitchfork. Instead, he repeatedly pointed to the Cowboys' mistakes on Sunday as an opportunity for Schottenheimer and his staff to learn and get better with 14 games remaining in the regular season.

He took this tack with the decision for Brandon Aubrey to send the ensuing kickoff through the end zone for a touchback rather than putting the ball in play to force a return. The touchback gave Baltimore the ball at the Dallas 35-yard line without burning any game clock.

"You can do a better job of what we were doing at that time," Jones said. "… That decision of how to do that kickoff. Trust me, that thing and the nuances on the sideline, the nuances and the input of everybody's decision there. That's being gone over with a fine-tooth comb."

Then there was the defensive coverage that allowed Lamar Jackson to find Zay Flowers on a 27-yard gain and call a timeout with one second remaining on the game clock. This play set up Ravens kicker Tyler Loop for his game-winning 56-yard field goal.

"We obviously didn't plan on that layer of receivers — that layer, the layer that got them in that good of position — we didn't plan on that layer of receivers catching the ball," Jones said.

Jones won't ask Schottenheimer to relinquish play-calling

It wasn't just one of these mistakes, but the combination of them all that allowed the Ravens to win the game in regulation. And it prompted a fair question to Jones. Does Schottenheimer have too much on his plate and should he delegate his offensive play-calling duties to better focus on game management?

Jones said that that decision will be left to Schottenheimer.

"I've always had the coach self-correct or self-adjust," Jones said. "Your coach is the first one — the head coach — is the first one to think adjusting if he's overloaded."

So this is where Jones is with Schottenheimer. He's calling for accountability while maintaining a line that Schottenheimer and his staff will learn and improve from their mistakes.

"We will be better from this experience that we had with Baltimore and what happened to us at the end of the game," Jones said. "We will be better because of it."

Don't expect Jones to have a short leash with Schottenheimer

This is a line that Jones frequently takes, often to the chagrin of Cowboys fans. He's historically been slower to move on from a head coach than the fan base would like.

After three weeks, he's certainly not ready to entertain firing Schottenheimer.

Jones has only fired a coach midseason one time in his 38 years as Cowboys owner, and he's said since that decision to fire Wade Phillips in 2010 that he regretted it . He's going to give Schottenheimer time to adjust.

But correctly or not, this is a Cowboys team that entered the season with Super Bowl hopes. A fan base that bought into those hopes isn't going to have the same sort of patience with Schottenheimer if things don't turn around quickly.

articles.title: Jim Harbaugh Backs OC Mike McDaniel Despite Chargers' 0-3 Start, Justin Herbert's Struggles
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Chargers are off to a 0-3 start to the season, and the offense has been one of the biggest issues.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Chargers are off to a 0-3 start to the season, and the offense has been one of the biggest issues.

But head coach Jim Harbaugh still has full trust in new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel. Harbaugh was asked after a 24-16 loss to the Buffalo Bills if he would consider relieving McDaniel of some of his control if the offense doesn't improve.

"No, we trust Mike. We believe in Mike," Harbaugh told reporters .

As the head coach of the Miami Dolphins, McDaniel crafted some of the NFL's best offenses in recent memory, but he hasn't brought that same success to Los Angeles.

The Chargers rank in the bottom half of the NFL in yards per game (308.7) and are averaging the fourth-fewest points per game (14.7) through three games. Quarterback Justin Herbert has struggled tremendously to start the season, recording 627 passing yards, three touchdowns and four interceptions.

He had his best game of the season against the Bills on Sunday but still managed just 226 yards, a touchdown and an interception.

The Chargers clearly need something to change on offense, but for now, Harbaugh will allow McDaniel to maintain control.

articles.title: NFL Brazil Game Nabs Record Audience
articles.summary: CBS said that the game averaged 24.9 million viewers.
articles.body:
CBS Sports's coverage last Sunday of a Ravens-Cowboys game from Rio de Janeiro made history on multiple fronts, extending the NFL's viewership resurgence.

The network said late Tuesday that the game averaged 24.9 million viewers, making it the most-watched NFL international game in records going back to the late 1980s. It also was the most-watched Week 3 game for CBS since 2014.

The game from Brazil was set up for ratings success in several ways. The broadcast was purposely scheduled in a national late-Sunday afternoon slot , traditionally the NFL's most-watched window. That placement diverged from the NFL's typical practice of staging international games in either early-morning or primetime windows for U.S. audiences.

Rio de Janeiro is only one hour ahead of the U.S. Eastern time zone, allowing much more schedule flexibility than games played in Europe or Australia.

Sunday's audience metrics were also likely boosted by a serious nor'easter that hit much of the highly populated U.S. Northeast corridor. Additionally, the Ravens-Cowboys game ended after MLB's final regular-season games and after that league's playoff field was set .

The CBS Sports broadcast highlighted another strong week for NFL viewership. Among the other Week 3 highlights:

Amazon Prime Video averaged 16.8 million viewers for the Thursday Night Football coverage of a Falcons-Packers game, up 2% from the comparable game in 2025. The online retail and streaming giant is off to its best viewership start since it gained exclusive TNF rights in 2022.

Through three weeks, CBS is averaging 19 million viewers for its NFL coverage, up 6% from the comparable period in a record-setting 2025 and supporting the network's bullishness heading into this season.

Those figures continue the historic upswell seen during Week 2 and further reverse the 13% viewership decline from Week 1 . Full audience data from Week 3 games will be released Thursday.

NBC Sports was a slight aberration from the larger trend, averaging 20.8 million viewers for its Sunday Night Football game between the Broncos and Rams, down 18% from a comparable Week 3 game last year between the Giants and Chiefs, perennially one of the NFL's most-watched teams. Still, each of the network's first four NFL games has topped 20 million in average viewership for the third straight season.

articles.title: Why Former NFL Player Called Bears Coach Ben Johnson an ‘Absolute Psychopath’

articles.body:
Former NFL player Emmanuel Acho praised Chicago Bears coach Ben Johnson for the aggressive approach that helped produce a convincing victory over the Philadelphia Eagles . Acho's strong assessment came after Johnson's creative play-calling repeatedly kept the Eagles defense off balance throughout the game.

Johnson's offensive strategy featured an assortment of formations, motions and play designs that created opportunities for Chicago's offense. The Bears consistently found ways to attack Philadelphia's defense, allowing them to control stretches of the game while building a comfortable advantage.

The performance highlighted Johnson's willingness to make unconventional decisions when opportunities presented themselves. Rather than relying on predictable sequences, Chicago repeatedly changed its approach and used different concepts to force the Eagles to adjust throughout the contest.

That level of creativity has become one of the defining characteristics of Johnson's offense. His ability to combine formations, personnel groupings and play-action concepts has given Chicago another dimension, while his willingness to remain aggressive has helped the Bears generate explosive opportunities.

Acho shared his thoughts about Johnson after Chicago won their Week 3 match . This can be seen in a post he made on X.

The result was a 27-7 victory that showcased how effective the offensive system can be when the players execute Johnson's plans. Chicago's performance against Philadelphia also demonstrated the potential of an offense capable of attacking defenses from multiple angles instead of relying on one particular formula.

Acho's colorful description reflected the level of admiration generated by Johnson's approach rather than criticism of the coach. If Chicago continues producing performances built around the same creativity and aggression, Johnson's play-calling could remain one of the team's biggest storylines as the season progresses.
